QUOTE: "In the default configuration it expands to `private_##member`, so a public struct field is renamed... The field is still in the header, but its name is changed, so code that reaches into it by the plain name fails to compile. C has no access control, so this rename is the only barrier."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the opacity comes from renaming the member so plain-name access fails to compile, and that the field stays in the header, which is the mechanism the item requires.
